newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans warn of disease in flooded border regions.
newsitem.headline: Germans warn of disease in flooded border regions.

text.p: German authorities said on Sunday there was an acute danger of disease in the vast area along the Polish border where the River Oder burst through flood banks in early July.
Matthias Freude, head of Brandenburg state's environmental ministry, said that the receding flood waters were leaving behind dangerous bacteria that caused diarrhoea and other illnesses.
After the worst floods the region has seen this century, an intense heat wave was now fostering the spread of bacteria, he said.

Thousands of Germans who were forced to flee the flooding three weeks ago were allowed to go home as water levels on the Oder River continued to fall. They were being advised to wear rubber gloves and protective boots.
The dikes preventing the swollen river from gushing into the Oderbruch basin east of Berlin were no longer in danger of bursting, authorities said.
About 5,000 people were finally given the all-clear to return to their homes in the agricultural area on Germany's frontier with Poland, although many had already gone back home.

Heavy rains in early July caused the worst flooding the area has seen this century. Six villages were partially or totally submerged and 7,200 hectares (18,000 acres) were left inundated. Large tracts of farmland have been ruined.
Although the cost of the damage has yet to be calculated, officials fear it could run into billions of dollars.
The flooding created even more havoc in neighbouring Czech Republic and Poland, where more than 100 people died.

Of the 160 km (100 miles) of dikes which held back most of the water on the German side, 3.5 km (two miles) were destroyed and will have to be rebuilt and another five km (three miles) will need repairs, at a cost of at least 132 million marks ($72 million), state officials said.

On the other side of the Oder in the Polish town of Slubice, many of the 16,000 evacuees who fled the rising waters two weeks ago were also returning to their homes under bright sunshine, relieved that the battle with the Oder was won.
